# Build — writing `build.md` the organization's way

You are writing `projects/<PRJ>/intents/<NN-slug>/build.md`. Below is what the organization's lifecycle says about this step, the sections the
artifact must carry, and its template. The lifecycle policy is the authority; this is a copy of it.

## What the lifecycle says — Build

Template: `policies/reference/lifecycles/ai-sdlc/build.md`

Each task is one change request to the project branch. A person reviews and merges it. When every task has
merged, the agent drafts `build.md` — what shipped, every deviation from the plan and who approved it, and the
tests that ran — and its approval marks the intent built.

## What `build.md` must carry

Open with the template's front matter and the Status line `**Status:** DRAFT`. You never write APPROVED: gov
writes it when a person approves the change request and it merges.

Then every one of these sections, as a `##` heading, in this order:

- Task → issue → CR → commit
- Deviations from plan
- Tests run and results
- Shipped in

## The template — `policies/reference/lifecycles/ai-sdlc/build.md`

````markdown
---
domain: development
layer: spec
owner: <owner>
compliance: C01
status: draft
---

# Build <NN>: <title>

**Status:** DRAFT
<!-- One of: DRAFT · APPROVED by <who> <date> (<change request link>) · STALE (<why>).
     gov writes the APPROVED line when the change request is approved by a person and merged; never write it by hand. -->

Plan: [plan.md](plan.md)

## Task → issue → CR → commit
| Task | Issue | Change request | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| T01 | <link> | <link> | <sha> |

## Deviations from plan
<!-- Each deviation with who approved it. "none" when there were none. -->
- <deviation> — approved by <who> (<link>)

## Tests run and results
<Suites, counts and run links. Counted from the runs, never from a summary line.>

## Shipped in
<Filled at release: `releases/<unit>/<version>` — the deploy.md that names this intent.>
````
